title: Chloranthy Ring
snippet:
Chloranthy Ring -  Dark Souls II - ring - notes 
 notes : The Chloranthy Ring's Stamina regeneration boosting effect stacks with Green Blossom and Stamina recovery shields, such as the Slumbering Dragon Shield.

title: Chloranthy Ring
snippet:
Chloranthy Ring -  Dark Souls II - ring - lead 
 lead : The **Chloranthy Ring** is a ring in *Dark Souls II*.

title: Chloranthy Ring
snippet:
Chloranthy Ring -  Dark Souls II - ring - description 
 description : The ring is named for its decorative green blossom, but its luster has long since faded. Raises stamina recovery speed.

title: Chloranthy Ring
snippet:
Chloranthy Ring -  Dark Souls II - ring - effect 
 effect : Like its *Dark Souls* version, it boosts the Stamina regeneration speed.
Normal ring raises Stamina recovery speed by 15%.
+1 - Raises Stamina recovery speed by 20%.
+2 - Raises Stamina recovery speed by 25%.

title: Chloranthy Ring
snippet:
Chloranthy Ring -  Dark Souls II - ring - availability 
 availability : The Chloranthy Ring is found in a chest behind an illusory wall which can only be revealed through a nearby Pharros' Contraption in the room below the ballistae in the Forest of Fallen Giants.

There is also a Chloranthy Ring+1 in an iron chest on an overhead cliff in the misty part of the Shaded Woods. The chest can be found by traveling along the right side of the forest until reaching another iron chest, containing the Old Sun Ring. Moving past this chest will bring the player to a small, raised path in the rock, leading the player to the ring.

The +2 version of the Chloranthy Ring drops from the Executioner's Chariot when killed in NG+. This can also be done by burning a Bonfire Ascetic in the Undead Purgatory bonfire.

title: Executioner's Chariot
snippet:
Executioner's Chariot -  Dark Souls II - boss - attacks 
 attacks : (**Note**: These attacks are for the horse, as the rider doesn't have any attacks.)*
***Dark Breath**: Breathes a cloud of Dark flame at the player, slowly shifting left or right depending on the direction of the player. Normally uses this attack when the player is within melee range. Has a very slow turn rate, can be easily evaded and the opportunity used to attack it.
***Stomp**: Rears up on its hind legs, and crashes down on the player. Has moderate tracking, but can be evaded with good roll timing. Can be blocked with a shield.
***Headbutt**: The horse swings its head left or right, hitting the player for low damage. Usually executes this attack when the player is at close range, can be easily blocked.

title: Executioner's Chariot
snippet: Phase two begins when the chariot bashes into the gate. The horse will be free as the chariot is completely destroyed and the charioteer is killed. The horse is very easy to fight and behaves similarly as the Fang Boar from the first *Dark Souls*. The horse has a charge attack where it bashes you with its head, this move is unblockable and does damage through your shield. If you linger behind the horse for too long, it will kick at you with its hind legs. If you are in front of it for too long, it will stand up on its hind legs and bash downwards on you. If you are at a medium distance away, the horse will spew a Dark fog that is unblockable and does heavy damage through your shield.

title: Executioner's Chariot
snippet:
Executioner's Chariot -  Dark Souls II - boss - strategy 
 strategy : **Phase 1**: The key here is to rush towards each of the two Necromancers and take them out before the Skeletons can catch up, avoiding the Chariot by hiding in alcoves as you go along. Bring a high stability shield if you can't run directly from one Necromancer to the other. Once the second Necromancer is killed, take out the Skeletons. Let the Chariot kill them if you wish. After the Necromancers and the Skeletons have been taken out, run to the lever and pull it.

title: Executioner's Chariot
snippet:
Executioner's Chariot -  Dark Souls II - boss - fight_overview 
 fight_overview : There are two phases to this fight: the "chariot" phase and the "horse" phase.

As you enter the fog door, phase one begins. The chariot will circle around the arena and attempt to ram into you. This can be avoided by hiding in the openings along the walls, or with a well-timed roll. The corridor is littered with Skeletons that will continue to revive until the Necromancers, which are hiding in the gaps along the walls, are killed. The chariot progressively loses speed the more damage it is dealt, giving you more time between its laps to deal with the skeletons and necromancers.

title: Executioner's Chariot
snippet:
Executioner's Chariot -  Dark Souls II - boss - alternate_strategy_ranged_or_magic_users 
 alternate_strategy_ranged_or_magic_users : After entering the arena, the player can choose to rush the first Necromancer and clean up the Skeletons, allowing the player to take cover in an alcove. Each time the chariot comes around, a well cast spell or a well timed arrow can deal damage to the chariot (a good spell to use is Homing Crystal Soulmass or just a simple Homing Soulmass. After casting, stand in one of the alcoves and wait). When the boss gets down to about 1/3 to 1/5 of its health, the chariot will stop circling the arena, most likely surprising the player.

title: Executioner's Chariot
snippet:
Executioner's Chariot -  Dark Souls II - boss - description 
 description : The Executioner's Chariot attempts to run over the player when encountered. It barrels through whatever is in its path, whether friend or foe. Upon killing the charioteer, the chariot's horse acts much like a Fang Boar from the original *Dark Souls*.

title: Executioner's Chariot
snippet: There are two methods of approaching the first phase. The first is to make your way around the corridor to the other side of the pit and pull the lever, which will lower a gate the chariot will crash into. The second method is to continually hit it with ranged attacks until it reaches 25% of its health. At this point, the chariot will be unable to clear the gap and fall. It will dangle off the ledge helplessly until it is hit one final time, which will cause it to lose its grip and tumble into the pit. This method skips phase two entirely.

title: Executioner's Chariot
snippet:
Executioner's Chariot -  Dark Souls II - boss - summoning 
 summoning : In Scholar of the First Sin only, Creighton the Wanderer can be recruited as a phantom for this fight, once freed, and, if the player moves fast enough, the shade Bashful Ray may also join, which can help in keeping the skeletons at bay for a while.

title: Executioner's Chariot
snippet:
(**Note**: If you have the Yearn spell or some Alluring Skulls, this fight becomes almost trivial. Cast Yearn or toss a skull as soon as you enter the fog gate and the Skeletons will just ignore you, getting maimed by the Chariot. Find the first Necromancer and kill him quickly. Dispose of any of the three initial Skeletons left. Start running towards the lever. When you see the first Skeleton, cast Yearn again or throw another skull and move to the second Necromancer. After he and all the remaining Skeletons are dead, pull the lever for a very easy boss fight.)*

**Phase 2**: At the start of phase two, the horse will fall over. This is the perfect time to use magic or pyromancy that has a long cast time for big damage. You don't want the horse to hit you as it does heavy damage and can deal damage through shields.

title: Executioner's Chariot
snippet: This strategy will end the same way as the caster version. Once the bosses health is low enough, it will miss the jump and end up hanging off the pit. Walk up and hit it once to finish the fight.

title: Executioner's Chariot
snippet: Circle around the horse and don't get too far away from it or it might use its breath attack which deals a lot of damage (but is easily dodged). Do not stay in front of the horse. Instead, stay behind it and try to bait it into kicking with its hind legs. Once it kicks and you successfully avoid it, move in quickly and hit the horse one or two times. The horse will then turn towards you and you should circle around it once again. You may also try to bait it into doing its front stomp attack or dodging its breath attack and then getting a few blows in. You don't want it to charge you as it is more difficult to dodge and can deal serious damage.

title: Executioner's Chariot
snippet:
Executioner's Chariot -  Dark Souls II - boss - trivia 
 trivia : The Executioner's Chariot was originally named the Silver Chariot in the network test. This name was probably a reference to the manga *JoJo's Bizarre Adventure/JoJo no Kimyou na Bouken.*

title: Executioner's Chariot
snippet:
Executioner's Chariot -  Dark Souls II - boss - lore 
 lore : The Executioner's Chariot was created with the sole purpose of tormenting and punishing the undead during the hunts organized by the Old Iron King. Although the Executioner appears to be the master of the chariot, it's actually the horse that controls the machine and carries out its creator's will to torture the undead.

title: Executioner's Chariot
snippet:
Executioner's Chariot -  Dark Souls II - boss - lead 
 lead : The **Executioner's Chariot** is a boss in *Dark Souls II*.

title: Executioner's Chariot
snippet:
Continuing around the arena, clearing out the remaining Necromancer and Skeletons, the player will notice that the chariot is being held above the pit by the two horses, while the charioteer dangles helplessly underneath. The player can now freely kill the boss without any resistance. A single attack will send the chariot tumbling into the abyss, finishing the boss fight.

If you are having trouble catching the Chariot as it goes by, try using a spell that shoots straight (like Lightning Spear or Soul Spear). Stand by one of the alcoves near the entrance to the boss fight and shoot it down the hall when you see the Chariot come around the corner. After you shoot it, you have plenty of time to dodge into the alcove. You can also use the binoculars if you like.

title: Executioner's Chariot
snippet:
Executioner's Chariot -  Dark Souls II - boss - notes 
 notes : The horse acts like a Fang Boar from the previous *Dark Souls*, with the exception of having a forward stomp and a dark breath attack.
The charge attack cannot be blocked, making dodging the only option.
The lever can be difficult to see but it's on the opposite side of the last Necromancer at an angle.
After defeating the boss, the player is given access to the Undead Purgatory bonfire and Titchy Gren.
In order to fight this boss again via a Bonfire Ascetic, making it NG+, you must burn the Ascetic at the Undead Purgatory bonfire.
It's possible to get past the Chariot without going into the alcoves by sticking to a wall and rolling when the chariot is about to hit the player. This requires near-perfect timing and can be made easier with a higher Adaptability stat.
Stacking Dark resistance makes surviving being run over by the chariot easier, as most of the chariot's attacks are Dark based.

title: Executioner's Chariot
snippet:
***Headbutt**: The horse swings its head left or right, hitting the player for low damage. Usually executes this attack when the player is at close range, can be easily blocked.
***Back Kick**: Using its hind legs to kick the player, normally if the player is near its rear or side arc. Unblockable and deals high damage and knockback, but has relatively short range and can be evaded by backing away.
***Charge**: The horse lowers both its heads, then charges at the player. Unblockable and deals high damage and knockback. It can perform this attack at any range, but the attack can be dodged by rolling to the side, giving players an opportunity to counterattack.
Defenses (Stats are from Param Studio and are not estimated)
Strike/Slash/Thrust defense are applied on top of Physical Defense.

title: Executioner's Chariot
snippet: Executioner's Chariot -  Dark Souls II - boss - alternate_strategy_melee

title: Executioner's Chariot
snippet: alternate_strategy_melee : A version of the above strategy is also available for melee builds. Proceed as normal, working your way up the arena, and killing the two Necromancers, letting the chariot take care of the Skeletons (Alluring Skulls work well here). Once you kill the last Necromancer, instead of pulling the lever, wait for the chariot to pass and run to the edge of the pit. Stand with your back against the right hand wall, facing the opposite wall, and as close to the edge of the pit as you can safely be. Since the chariot is jumping, it cannot hit you here. Each time it lands you can take a swing at it, and whittle down its health bar. This works with most weapons, but a weapon with a wide swing is better as locking on is a very bad idea. The timings will vary, so some experimentation will be necessary. As an example, a Greatsword R1, triggered the instant the boss jumps will always connect and do decent damage.

title: Executioner's Chariot
snippet:
Executioner's Chariot -  Dark Souls II - boss - location 
 location : Found in the Undead Purgatory, past the great hanging bridge at Huntsman's Copse.

In *Scholar of the First Sin*, a chariot horse can be found in Drangleic Castle, in the hall previously filled with Alonne Knight Captains.

title: Explorer
snippet:
For restocking the items, Merchant Hag Melentia carries more Lifegems and Witching Urns and 1 more Pharros' Lockstone, Laddersmith Gilligan has Aromatic Oozes, Wood Bolts are sold by Blacksmith Lenigrast, Repair Powders are sold in limited quantities by Blacksmiths and infinitely by one late-game merchant, Prism Stones are sold by Sweet Shalquoir, and 5 more Rusted Coins are sold by Magerold of Lanafir.

Their high Adaptability gives them 9 i-frames when starting out, and they only need 2 more points in the stat to improve that to 10 i-frames.

title: Explorer
snippet:
The Traveling Merchant Set is only a bit better than the Imported Set and has no Poise but the hat increases Item Discovery slightly, which is a solid benefit early on.

The lone Pharros' Lockstone can be used to unlock 1 (and only one, since it is a consumable) Pharros' Contraption. Of the first two Contraptions to be found in the game, the first one is below a trapped room with ballistae in the Forest of Fallen Giants and used to get the Chloranthy Ring and a Titanite Slab, and the second one is found one a small platform up halfway up the first set of stairs in No-man's Wharf where it is used turn on the lights and scare away all the Dark Stalkers in the area.

title: Explorer
snippet:
Explorer -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Explorer** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 2*.

It has no particular specialty, with only high Adaptability and an above average Vitality being notable. It is, essentially, a Deprived with some extra stats, some bonus items, and a Dagger.

As their Dagger is the only weapon they start out with, with not even a spell to help them, it is imperative to pick up a second Dagger in Things Betwixt on the first side path fore more Durability. Is is possible to wield the Morning Star from the cliffs in Majula two-handed with 2 more points in Strength and one more point in Dexterity, and a Light Crossbow can be found atop a wall in the Forest of Fallen Giants and only need 1 more point in Strength to wield with two hands.

The Traveling Merchant Set is only a bit better than the Imported Set and has no Poise but the hat increases Item Discovery slightly, which is a solid benefit early on.

title: Explorer
snippet:
Explorer -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - starting_equipment 
 starting_equipment : The Explorer also starts with a variety of items: a Spell Quartz Ring, 20 Wood Bolts, 8 Witching Urns, 4 Aromatic Oozes, 5 Prism Stones, 2 Rusted Coins, 1 Repair Powder, and 1 Pharros' Lockstone.

As with all starting classes in Dark Souls 2, the Imported Set worn before the character creation can be found unequipped in the character's inventory.

title: Havel's Ring
snippet:
Havel's Ring -  Dark Souls - ring - effects 
 effects : Raises the player's maximum equipment burden by 50%.

title: Havel's Ring
snippet:
Havel's Ring -  Dark Souls - ring - availability 
 availability : Havel the Rock drops this ring when killed. He can either be accessed through a door in the latter half of the Undead Burg through use of the Master Key, or accessed through a door just prior to the Hydra in the Darkroot Basin.

title: Havel's Ring
snippet:
Havel's Ring -  Dark Souls - ring - description 
 description : This ring was named after Havel the Rock, Lord Gwyn's old battlefield compatriot.

Havel's men wore the ring to express faith in their leader and to carry a heavier load.

title: Havel's Ring
snippet:
Havel's Ring -  Dark Souls - ring - lead 
 lead : **Havel's Ring** is a ring in *Dark Souls*.

title: Havel's Ring
snippet:
Havel's Ring -  Dark Souls - ring - overview 
 overview : Havel's Ring is one of the first rings accessible to the player assuming the Master Key was chosen as the starting gift. It is a useful ring, allowing many classes to upgrade from slow roll to mid roll or better and giving players a wider range of equipment options without sacrificing mobility. Later, the player may want to invest in Endurance to free up their ring slot, although certain players may require both the ring and high endurance if they seek out the heavier weapons and armor. Prior to patch 1.06 Havel's ring was inferior in many ways to the Dark Wood Grain Ring, but the two rings can be combined to use most of the game's equipment with ease.

title: Heavy Armor Sets (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Heavy Armor Sets (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - mechanic - lead 
 lead : For categorization purposes on this wiki, **heavy armor sets** are armor sets in *Dark Souls* that have a total weight of 40 or more.

Wearing heavy armor will slightly reduce the player's stamina regeneration, along with certain pieces of other armor sets. Each piece of heavy armor will reduce the stamina regeneration rate by 2 per second for all body armor pieces, and 1 per second for all other pieces. Furthermore, if the player has an equipment load that is higher than 50%, they will suffer a further 20% stamina regeneration penalty. Using Havel's Ring allows one to increase their equipment load, allowing them to wear Heavy Armor more easily.

title: Kingseeker Frampt
snippet:
If players have given Kaathe the Lordvessel already, then it is possible to prevent Frampt from leaving by rushing around and away from him. As long as he doesn't finish his dialogue, he won't disappear. Players can also prevent him finishing his dialogue by attacking him.
It's actually possible to kill Kingseeker Frampt, but only through the use of third party programs. Frampt has 11,120 HP and drops 5,000 souls after being killed.
Frampt will randomly be found sleeping deeply (usually after resting at a bonfire) even if he was spoken to only moments ago. He can be awoken by attacking him (kicking and punching are sufficient).

title: Kingseeker Frampt
snippet:
Kingseeker Frampt -  Dark Souls - character - location 
 location : Firelink Shrine, where the pool in front of the decrepit statue used to be. Kingseeker Frampt only appears after the Bells of Awakening have been rung.

title: Kingseeker Frampt

 services : Kingseeker Frampt has the ability to consume items and break titanite into smaller pieces.

title: Kingseeker Frampt
snippet:
Kingseeker Frampt -  Dark Souls - character - plot 
 plot : Kingseeker Frampt appears in Firelink Shrine after the player rings both Bells of Awakening. He instructs the player to go to Anor Londo and obtain the Lordvessel. After the player obtains the Lordvessel, Frampt transports them to the entrance of the Kiln of the First Flame, and instructs the player to place the Lordvessel to gain access to the Kiln, and to ultimately kill Gwyn and prolong the Age of Fire.

Should the player give the Lordvessel to Kaathe instead, Frampt will become irate and leave the player for the rest of the playthrough.

title: Kingseeker Frampt
snippet:
Kingseeker Frampt -  Dark Souls - character - feed 
 feed : Feeding weapons and armor to him is not very profitable; most weapons only produce 50 souls while most armor produces 100. Special weapons can produce much more, such as the Drake Sword, which results in 5,000.

title: Kingseeker Frampt
snippet:
Kingseeker Frampt -  Dark Souls - character - removed_content 
 removed_content : The following is content that is present within the code of *Dark Souls*, but not actually implemented in the game. Text was found from a text dump which can be found at: http://pastebin.com/hA42TwK8.

title: Kingseeker Frampt
snippet:
After ringing the first of the Bells of Awakening, Frampt can be heard snoring when passing through the flooded area of Firelink Shrine of which he will eventually emerge. Strangely, this makes a collectible, invisible "humanity sprite" (one that increases your character's liquid humanity by 1 point) spawn nearby. It is possible to collect this sprite by falling from the nest above or one of the ledges above, but the fall may kill the character in the process (forcing the player to run back to his bloodstain from the last bonfire they rested at). It is also possible to collect this sprite by "passing through" Frampt's room. It seems to often be near the fallen pillar that lays diagonally on the ground (one end of the pillar pointing to the starting Lordran Bonfire of Firelink Shrine, and the other end of the pillar pointing to the graveyard leading to the Catacombs).
Frampt is one of the few characters whose mouth moves when talking.

title: Kingseeker Frampt
snippet:
Kingseeker Frampt -  Dark Souls - character - trivia 
 trivia : Shortly after Frampt's arrival, the Crestfallen Warrior (who sits fairly close to Frampt) complains about a horrible smell. This is likely referring to Frampt. The Crestfallen Warrior will leave after being spoken to when Frampt is around, so keep that in mind before ringing the second bell of awakening. The Crestfallen Warrior can later be found as a hostile Hollow at the New Londo Ruins.
In previous versions of the game there was a glitch where if a player jumped down the hole Frampt sticks his head out of, but quit and loaded before reaching the bottom, they would reach the Kiln of the First Flame. In doing so players could skip gathering the Lord Souls and go straight to the fight against Gwyn. This technique has been used for speedruns of the game.

title: Kingseeker Frampt
snippet:
Kingseeker Frampt -  Dark Souls - character - lead 
 lead : is a character in *Dark Souls*. He is a primordial serpent who seeks a human successor to Gwyn, Lord of Cinder. He is voiced by Peter Marinker, who also voiced Darkstalker Kaathe and Eingyi.

title: Kingseeker Frampt
snippet:
Frampt is one of the few characters whose mouth moves when talking.
On the breastplate of Lord Gwyn's Robes, there are patterns and indents that resemble Frampt's head. Possibly as an indicator of their friendship, as mentioned by Kaathe.
It would seem Frampt has a great dislike of Executioner Smough, Seath the Scaleless and his followers. If fed any of their items, he will only give a single soul in exchange.

title: Kingseeker Frampt
snippet:
Kingseeker Frampt -  Dark Souls - character - notes 
 notes : When Frampt transports the player to the Firelink Altar after retrieving the Lordvessel, it is not necessary to place it. By using a Homeward Bone or the Homeward miracle, it is possible to exit and continue using Frampt's feeding service and at the same time interact with Kaathe and join the Darkwraiths. As long as the player does not place the Lordvessel, neither serpent will depart.
The player should avoid attacking Frampt (unless he is asleep) as it may result in him leaving for the rest of the playthrough. If this happens, the player loses access to his feeding service and must either place the Lordvessel with Kaathe or do it alone by dropping down the hole Frampt was in.
Dropping down to the Firelink Altar after acquiring the Lordvessel without his help will make Frampt leave, whether the player placed it or not.

title: Knight Lautrec of Carim
snippet:
Knight Lautrec of Carim -  Dark Souls - character - strategy 
 strategy : Lautrec dual-wields Shotels, allowing him to partially hit through block. Therefore, dodging his attacks or killing him as quickly as possible will work best. He also wears a Red Tearstone Ring, so be extra careful when he is near-death. Additionally, he may use a [https://darksouls.wiki.fextralife.com/Parrying+dagger parrying dagger] to parry and riposte players.

If fought at Firelink Shrine, Lautrec can safely be kicked off the ledge. Quit and load the game, and his items should be right in front of the player.

title: Knight Lautrec of Carim
snippet:
Knight Lautrec of Carim -  Dark Souls - character - lead 
 lead : **Knight Lautrec of Carim** (女神の騎士ロートレク), also known as **Lautrec the Embraced** or **Lautrec the Guilty** when invading, is a character in *Dark Souls*. He is voiced by either Daniel Roberts or Will Vanderpuye.

title: Knight Lautrec of Carim
snippet: A very easy way to defeat him consists of wearing both the Ring of Fog and the Slumbering Dragoncrest Ring. The player must then approach him and his companions by walking along either of the hall's walls until they reach the area behind him, then they may approach him from behind and backstab him. If the player's weapon is strong enough, a single backstab will suffice. Even if he survives, his two comrades will not react as they are slightly in front of him, allowing the player to finish the job. Once behind Lautrec, the Ring of Fog can be switched for the Hornet Ring to increase the damage. One can also use Hush to remove the need of the Slumbering Dragoncrest Ring, although they must be careful not to move after the effect expires.

title: Knight Lautrec of Carim
snippet:
Knight Lautrec of Carim -  Dark Souls - character - notes 
 notes : Once Reah and her bodyguards Vince and Nico leave Firelink Shrine and Petrus has returned from the trip, Lautrec will offer a tip to the player at the cost of 100 souls per soul level, in which he informs that they went "below the Catacombs" and that her bodyguards either fled or were reduced to hollows, leaving her alone; hinting to travel to the Tomb of the Giants and investigate their whereabouts.
Lautrec's armor, the Set of Favor, will appear on the same level as the Chamber of the Princess bonfire room, after the player has killed him in Anor Londo.
Up to 4 liquid humanities (8 in NG+) can be drained from Lautrec using the Dark Hand.

title: Knight Lautrec of Carim
snippet:
Up to 4 liquid humanities (8 in NG+) can be drained from Lautrec using the Dark Hand.
Lautrec is a useful summon to keep around, should the player be wandering a high-traffic PvP area, as his Shotels make an excellent distraction. Should the invader focus their attacks on the player, Lautrec has a chance of attacking from behind for a backstab. Lautrec is also extremely good at both parries and dodge-rolls for an NPC, which means aggressive invaders can find themselves countered at a bad moment. On higher difficulties, his HP is substantially higher, making him a go-to PvP ally for the Parish and Depths.
To summon Lautrec for the Bell Gargoyles, the player must first free him then talk to him in Firelink Shrine and rest at a bonfire for his summon sign to appear.
If Lautrec is killed in Undead Parish without talking to him, the cell door becomes permanently locked from being opened.

title: Knight Lautrec of Carim
snippet:
Knight Lautrec of Carim -  Dark Souls - character - lore 
 lore : Lautrec's armor reveals that he was an adherent of the goddess Fina. The armor description states that Lautrec, during a period of solitude, "forsook everything" because he believed in Fina's love for him. This could either mean that Lautrec was delusional, or that the goddess emotionally manipulated him, as it is mentioned in Ring of Favor and Protection that Fina has a “fateful beauty”.

Lautrec's goals were never explained in the game. He mentions that he is on a "mission", yet it is never elaborated upon. He interacted with, and was possibly tricked by Patches at least once prior to meeting the player, and he knows of Petrus and his background. It could be that Anastacia was killed for her Fire Keeper Soul, but it is found on his person after defeating him, meaning he either had neglected to use it or kept it as a trophy.

title: Knight Lautrec of Carim
snippet:
If fought at Firelink Shrine, Lautrec can safely be kicked off the ledge. Quit and load the game, and his items should be right in front of the player.

If fought in Anor Londo, Lautrec will have a sorcerer and a Pike-wielding warrior guarding him. The player is only required to kill Lautrec, so they may choose to concentrate on him and hope to kill him before his companions cause any trouble. An easy way to do this is to go up the staircases to the left or right, then aggro Lautrec with a bow. Lautrec is faster than the rest of his party and will run up the stairs first, which then allows the player to engage him alone atop the chokepoint.

Poison Arrows can prove effective on both Lautrec and his companions. In addition, firing them from where the player spawns in his world will not make them aggro. This lets the player kill without retaliation.

title: Knight Lautrec of Carim
snippet:
Knight Lautrec of Carim -  Dark Souls - character - location 
 location : Lautrec is found imprisoned on the top floor of the church in Undead Parish, before climbing the ladders to the roof where the Bell Gargoyles are fought. The Mystery Key that opens his cell (which can also be opened with the Master Key) is found in the cellar-like area next to the Fang Boar guarding the gates to the inner parish.

After being freed, or escaping after the Gargoyles are defeated if he wasn't freed by the player, Lautrec is found sitting in Firelink Shrine across from the imprisoned Fire Keeper, Anastacia of Astora. If Lautrec was freed, then it is here that he will reward the player with a Sunlight Medal.

title: Knight Lautrec of Carim
snippet:
If the player frees Lautrec and receives his reward at Firelink Shrine, he can be summoned to assist against the Bell Gargoyles and the Gaping Dragon. His first summon sign is near the ladder before the Fog Door; the second summon is opposite from Solaire's, hidden behind a pillar near the Gaping Dragon's fog door.

Whether or not Lautrec was freed, after the player rings the second Bell of Awakening or picks up the Fire Keeper Soul in Blighttown, Lautrec will kill Anastacia and begin a quest line in which the player can collect a Black Eye Orb along with Anastacia's robes, and hunt Lautrec down to retrieve the Fire Keeper's Soul in Anor Londo.

title: Knight Lautrec of Carim
snippet:
Knight Lautrec of Carim -  Dark Souls - character - trivia 
 trivia : Lautrec is likely a spiritual successor to Yurt from *Demon's Souls*. Both are found imprisoned and the player can rescue them, both use shotels and parrying daggers, and both are hostile towards the player later in the game. They even share identical quotes such as, *"Now I can continue my work...keh heh heh"*.
Lautrec, like many characters, has unused dialogue cut from the game.

title: Ring of Favor and Protection
snippet:
Ring of Favor and Protection -  Dark Souls - ring - description 
 description : A ring symbolizing the favor and protection of the goddess Fina, known in legend to possess "fateful beauty".

This ring boosts its wearer's HP, stamina, and max equipment load, but breaks if ever removed.

title: Ring of Favor and Protection
snippet:
Ring of Favor and Protection -  Dark Souls - ring - general_information 
 general_information : When worn, the Ring of Favor and Protection increases the player's maximum HP, Stamina and equipment load by 20%. The item is destroyed, however, if it is ever removed.

After the player reaches 40 Endurance, wearing the Ring of Favor and Protection is the only way to further increase maximum Stamina.

title: Ring of Favor and Protection
snippet:
Ring of Favor and Protection -  Dark Souls - ring - trivia 
 trivia : Swapping a Ring of Favor and Protection with another Ring of Favor and Protection does not cause either to break. Moving the ring between ring slots will also not break the ring.

title: Ring of Favor and Protection
snippet:
Ring of Favor and Protection -  Dark Souls - ring - notes 
 notes : The Ring of Favor and Protection stacks with other equipment burden/max HP items, such as Havel's Ring and Mask of the Father.

title: Ring of Favor and Protection
snippet:
Ring of Favor and Protection -  Dark Souls - ring - overview 
 overview : This ring is useful for players that are absolutely sure that they would never require another ring slot, or if they temporarily require a boost in vitality and stamina. However, removing the ring (and thus breaking it) is ill-advised since only two of them can be obtained per playthrough.

In PvP, many builds rely on the Ring of Favor and Protection to don heavier armor without sacrificing the fast roll, and the extra HP—essentially granting players the equivalent of extra soul levels without actually leveling up. Players are conversely limiting the diversity of rings they can use, however. The Hornet Ring, Havel's Ring and the Bellowing Dragoncrest Ring are all examples of rings that players could otherwise use had they not equipped the Ring of Favor and Protection with the intent of not breaking it.

 upgrading : Like weapons, most but not all armor pieces can be upgraded. Armor can be upgraded to +10 or to +5 for those that require Twinkling Titanite. Armor cannot be upgraded down other upgrade paths. Upgraded armor yields higher defensive values and elemental resistance, but never alters Poise.

title: Bandit (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Bandit (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Bandit** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 2*.

It has high Dexterity and well above average Faith, meaning it lends itself rather well towards builds focused either on both or only the former (though it will have strong competition from the Swordsman when it comes to pure Dexterity builds). It is rather unsuitable to spells, even the Miracle ones, due to its extremely low Attunement and Intelligence.

Bandits are actually unable to speak to Straid of Olaphis by default, the only class that can't do that, due to its extremely low Intelligence not meeting his minimum required amount of 3.

title: Bandit (Dark Souls II)
snippet: There is a curious disadvantage to its high Vitality, higher than any other starting class: when using the Third Dragon Ring, it cannot receive the full benefit of the Flynn's Ring and will get a light decrease of 4 Attack Rating compared to any other class.

title: Bandit (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Until an unlimited source of arrows is acquired, they are best either saved for trying to pull individual enemies from groups or ambushes, or for trying to kill one of the early Ogres (either the one outside the Firekeeper's Hut in Things Betwixt at the start of the tutorial that also holds the Stone Ring, or the Scholar of the First Sin-exclusive one on the way towards the Forest of Fallen Giants) for a large amount of extra Souls.

The class's Bandit Set is actually fairly good, as it has somewhat high physical defences and is, together with the Knight's partial Falconer Set, the only starting set with decent starting Poise.

Due to its very low Adaptability and Attunement it has a substandard roll (only 7 i-frames, compared to most other classes having 8 or 9 i-frames) and needs 3 points in Adaptability or 9 points in Attunement to improve this to 8 i-frames.

title: Bandit (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Bandits are actually unable to speak to Straid of Olaphis by default, the only class that can't do that, due to its extremely low Intelligence not meeting his minimum required amount of 3.

The starting weapons are somewhat mixed, with the Short Bow following the higher starting value in Dexterity while the Hand Axe instead focuses on Strength. The Hand Axe is most likely better replaced with an actually Dexterity-focused weapon, though those are in limited supply until Blacksmith Lenigrast's shop is opened, mostly the Dagger in Things Betwixt and the Halberd in the Forest of Fallen Giants. Beyond extra weapons such as the Spear and the Rapier, Lenigrast also holds the game's first infinite supply of ammunition (merely more Wood Arrows, but still) and another Short Bow.

snippet: The Mask of the Father's burden increase perk stacks with those of other items: Havel's Ring (+50% equip burden) and the Ring of Favor and Protection (+20%). title: Endurance (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Endurance (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - mechanic - equipment_load 
 equipment_load : Equipment load determines how much equipment the player can equip before being affected by movement penalties. The softcap for endurance is 40 in terms of carry weight. The Mask of the Father, Havel's Ring, and Ring of Favor and Protection also improve equipment load. Though Mask of the Father is so heavy it usually cancels out its own effect.

title: Stamina (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Stamina (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - mechanic - modifiers 
 modifiers : The player's maximum stamina can be raised by increasing the endurance stat while leveling up, until reaching 160 stamina at 40 endurance. Increasing endurance past 40 does not further affect the maximum stamina.

The only other way to raise the maximum stamina is equipping the Ring of Favor and Protection, which raises maximum stamina by 20%. By having both 40 endurance and the Ring of Favor and Protection equipped, the player's maximum stamina can be raised to a total of 192 points.

title: Lingering Dragoncrest Ring (Dark Souls III)
snippet:

The ring reduces the decay rate of the buff while it is worn. This means that the ring must be constantly equipped in order to benefit from the increased duration.

title: Heavy Armor Sets (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Heavy Armor Sets (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - armor - characteristics 
 characteristics : Heavy armor sets provide the strongest defenses and the most Poise. However, they are also extremely costly in weight, meaning that the wearer must invest heavily in Vitality if they intend to use heavy armor.

Because of the high absorption values and the great amount of Poise provided, heavy armor is ideal protection for players who intend to equip ultra weapons and perform Hyper Armor trades with opponents. Ultra weapons tend to weigh a lot and cost tremendous amounts of stamina to swing, so equipment such as Havel's Ring and Chloranthy Ring tend to go hand-in-hand with such builds.

Because virtually all heavy sets are plate metal-based, most sets in this category tend to be weak to Strike damage and Lightning attacks, though exceptions do exist. Their plate metal nature, however, also tends to make them highly resistant to Slash damage and Bleed buildup.

title: Equipment Load (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Equipment Load (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - mechanic - modifiers 
 modifiers : The primary modifier for the maximum equipment load is the stat endurance. The player character's maximum equip load equals 40 plus their endurance.

The following items can be used to further increase maximum equipment load:

The Mask of the Father increases the maximum equipment load by 5%.
The Ring of Favor and Protection increases the maximum equipment load by 20%.
Havel's Ring increases the maximum equipment load by 50%.

The effects of the items stack multiplicatively. Equipping all three items raises the maximum equipment load by a total of 89%.
